# Bug Catalog: `verify/tutorial_ability_onboarding.gd`

**Generated by the `design-tests` workflow on 2026-09-21**  
**Scope:** tutorial-to-world handoff across `game/battle.gd`, `game/world.gd`,
`game/diver.gd`, and the new ability-onboarding surface. The test exercises
the public player flow rather than a private implementation detail.

## What this slice does

The first tutorial battle teaches combat. This slice must hand a player back to
the explorable world with a short, navigable explanation of world controls and
each diver's actual exploration ability. It must pause the game while the
explanation is open, retain tutorial recovery paths, and restore normal
mouse/keyboard control when the player dismisses it.

## Public interface

| Symbol | Type | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Battle.finished(result)` | signal | Real tutorial-to-world completion boundary; result is `won`, `lost`, `fled`, or `skipped`. |
| `World._on_battle_finished(result)` | handoff | Restores the world after Battle and requests onboarding. |
| `Diver.can_use_ability()` | method | Defines whether an active diver can currently start an ability. |
| `Diver.ability_needs_aim()` | method | Defines grapple's extra aim-and-click step. |
| `Diver.toggle_sonar()` | method | Defines sonar's toggle and oxygen precondition. |
| `AbilityOnboarding.open_for_world(world)` | planned UI API | Opens a paged world-controls and ability walkthrough for the live party. |
| `AbilityOnboarding.advance_page()`, `go_back()`, `dismiss()` | planned UI API | Actions behind visible buttons and keyboard shortcuts. |
| `AbilityOnboarding.current_page_data()` | planned UI API | Provides the active page's content contract for test/accessibility checks. |

## Load-bearing comments and contracts read

- `World._start_ability()` routes swap to Left/Right/Enter selection,
  grapple to first-person aim then mouse click, and shockwave directly to an
  omnidirectional action.
- Environmental abilities do **not** consume oxygen; sonar is the one world
  ability with an oxygen cost. The walkthrough must not recreate the earlier
  misconception that grapple becomes unavailable at zero oxygen.
- The current tutorial has a forced QTE, disabled Run, explicit Skip, and
  win/loss/retry handoffs. This slice cannot replace any of those flows.
- `TutorialBook` documents the established modal contract: `PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS`,
  a full-rect overlay, a paused scene tree, and keyboard dismissal.

## IO boundaries

- **Scene tree/time:** `Battle.finished`, deferred world handoff, and
  `SceneTree.paused` are the asynchronous boundaries.
- **Input:** Enter/arrow/E/Tab/Q and mouse aim/click must map to wording the
  player sees.
- **Persistent state:** this first-run UI must not alter saves, stats,
  inventory, oxygen, or ability cooldowns.
- **No HTTP/filesystem/randomness:** this slice has none.

## Branching points examined

- `World._on_battle_finished`: `won`, `fled`, `skipped`, `lost`, and special
  encounter branches.
- `World._start_ability`: swap, aimed grapple, or immediate shockwave.
- `World._unhandled_input`: aim, target selection, menu escape, movement,
  camera, and ability keys.
- `Diver.toggle_sonar`: passive absent, toggle off, or toggle on with oxygen.
- Onboarding page index: first, middle, final, and dismissal states.

## Existing tests

- `verify/tutorial_exit.gd` proves Battle can finish and return to World, but
  not that a player receives world controls.
- `verify/tutorial_loss_choice.gd` proves Retry and Exit recover safely.
- `verify/tutorial_skip.gd` proves explicit Skip restores party and world.
- `verify/tutorial_qte.gd` proves the forced tutorial QTE is visible/solvable.
- `verify/swim.gd` proves mouse-look changes camera yaw in World.

## Bug catalog

| # | Bug (one sentence, failure mode) | Blast radius | Plausibility | Test type | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Completing the combat lesson returns the player directly to open water without explaining swim, diver switching, or world abilities. | High — a first-time player sees the game become aimless or broken immediately after the tutorial. | Was present in baseline: `World._on_battle_finished("won")` only announced completion. | Captured end-to-end contract | Fixed |
| 2 | An onboarding modal leaves the tree paused after dismissal, so the player cannot swim despite completing the tutorial. | High — soft-lock at the first free-play moment. | A paused-but-interactive UI is easy to wire incorrectly. | Round-trip invariant | Characterized |
| 3 | A page teaches controls that differ from live behavior, especially treating grapple/shockwave as oxygen-limited or omitting swap confirmation controls. | High — an otherwise working route appears broken. | Raw #72 text predates current environmental-oxygen and guardian work. | Data-to-behavior differential | Characterized |
| 4 | Forward/back navigation loses the current page or lets the final page advance into a blank page. | Medium — a player misses an ability or sees a broken Next button. | Raw #72 only had Next/Close; this slice adds Back navigation. | Decision-table contract | Characterized |
| 5 | Onboarding opens more than once for one resolution or opens during a loss Retry loop. | Medium — duplicate modals interrupt combat or force repeated reading. | Battle outcomes are asynchronous and loss has two explicit choices. | Negative-path end-to-end | Characterized |
| 6 | A tutorial caption can only be advanced with an undiscoverable keyboard key, leaving mouse-first players stalled despite a visible lesson. | High — first-time players can mistake waiting for input as a frozen game. | Was present in baseline: `_tutorial_show_step()` rendered only "Press Enter" text. | Captured UI interaction | Fixed |

## Test plan

### Bug #1 — missing ability handoff

- **Test type:** captured end-to-end contract.
- **Description string:**
  > `tutorial ability onboarding: a completed lesson opens world-control pages — guards against missing first-free-play handoff`
- **What it catches:** a real tutorial win removes Battle but gives no
  ability/control teaching before free play.
- **Self-critique:**
  - Could this pass for wrong-but-stable output? **No.** It requires a live
    tutorial win, a visible walkthrough, and the four promised page identities.
  - Could this fail under a behavior-preserving refactor? **No.** It uses
    public UI actions/page data and paused state, not child paths/callbacks.

### Bug #2 — pause-state leak

- **Test type:** round-trip invariant combined with Bug #1's real handoff.
- **Description string:**
  > `tutorial ability onboarding: dismiss resumes a steerable world — guards against paused-world soft-lock`
- **What it catches:** a close action that hides UI but fails to unpause World,
  or the opposite.
- **Self-critique:**
  - Could this pass for wrong-but-stable output? **No.** It checks open/closed
    state and the actual scene-tree paused state.
  - Could this fail under a behavior-preserving refactor? **No.** Any overlay
    implementation can satisfy the same observable contract.

### Bug #3 — stale ability instructions

- **Test type:** data-to-behavior differential.
- **Description string:**
  > `tutorial ability onboarding: every page matches the live ability contract — guards against stale controls and false oxygen costs`
- **What it catches:** wording/page metadata that no longer matches
  `Diver.BASE_STATS`, `World._start_ability`, or sonar's resource rule.
- **Self-critique:**
  - Could this pass for wrong-but-stable output? **No.** It compares each page's
    declared action metadata to live diver behavior.
  - Could this fail under a behavior-preserving refactor? **No.** It relies on
    stable player concepts, not label construction or widget layout.

### Bug #4 — incomplete navigation

- **Test type:** decision-table contract over first/middle/final page states.
- **Description string:**
  > `tutorial ability onboarding: next/back boundaries retain every lesson — guards against blank or unreachable pages`
- **What it catches:** missing Back, final-page overflow, or an accidental
  auto-dismiss before the last ability.
- **Self-critique:**
  - Could this pass for wrong-but-stable output? **No.** It traverses every
    page and asserts identities/boundaries.
  - Could this fail under a behavior-preserving refactor? **No.** It does not
    assert a widget tree.

### Bug #5 — duplicate/incorrect outcome timing

- **Test type:** negative-path end-to-end.
- **Description string:**
  > `tutorial ability onboarding: retry stays in the lesson and exit opens one handoff — guards against duplicate modal timing`
- **What it catches:** a modal that appears during Retry or multiple times on
  loss exit.
- **Self-critique:** deferred until the base public modal API is green, because
  it composes with the existing loss-choice contract.

### Bug #6 — keyboard-only tutorial continuation

- **Test type:** captured UI interaction.
- **Description string:**
  > `tutorial continue button: clicking the visible action advances the caption — guards against keyboard-only tutorial stalls`
- **What it catches:** a caption that asks a mouse-driven player to continue
  but has no clickable action, or a button that is visible but disconnected
  from the real narration wait state.
- **Self-critique:**
  - Could this pass for wrong-but-stable output? **No.** It waits for a real
    Battle tutorial caption, activates the visible button, and checks the
    actual wait flag synchronously clears.
  - Could this fail under a behavior-preserving refactor? **No.** It finds a
    named user-facing button and invokes its public `pressed` signal; it does
    not rely on a layout coordinate or private callback.

## Skipped

- Exact pulse opacity/frame timing — cosmetic and better covered by browser
  visual evidence than a brittle timing assertion.
- Copy-editing prose line by line — automated protection maps content metadata
  to real controls; readability is reviewed at narrow browser widths.
- Ability demonstration videos — the referenced media assets do not exist;
  text plus contextual controls must work first.
- Save persistence of onboarding completion — deferred until product decides
  whether first-run explanation should replay across sessions.

## Post-write evaluation

- **Bugs caught:** Bug #1 failed against baseline with `MISSING FIRST-FREE-PLAY
  HANDOFF`. Bug #6 then failed with `KEYBOARD-ONLY TUTORIAL STALL`.
- **Bugs characterized:** Bugs #2–#5 pass after the implementation: close
  restores the scene tree, all pages map to live ability behavior, boundaries
  work, and loss Retry does not open onboarding before Exit does.
- **Bugs discovered during writing:** raw #72 ability wording conflicts with
  current zero-oxygen environmental abilities; raw global-class lookup also
  fails this project's headless verification path, so World explicitly
  preloads the overlay script.
- **Tests removed:** none.
